executive_summary: Market enters Wednesday with two crosscurrents: AMD's earnings-night disappointment pressures the AI hardware complex, while index futures still lean green on Big Tech cash-flow leadership. WTI is bouncing off $100 as Hormuz tensions persist despite Trump's 'Project Freedom' initiative, keeping defense and integrated energy bid. The Fed is locked at 3.50-3.75% with the first 4-dissenter vote since 1992 — credibility risk is real, and the 10Y at 4.43% is the swing variable. Today's earnings test (UBER, KHC, NVO, FLUT) will drive single-name dispersion, but the macro print to watch is the May 12 CPI — energy is now the inflation-revision risk that delays any cut path further.

macro_events.title: AMD reports Q1; stock collapses ~14% AH on guidance
macro_events.causal_chain: AMD-Meta deal ($60B over 5 years) created elevated expectations -> Q1 revenue $9.84B in line but commentary on data-center linearity disappoints -> stock gaps -14% AH -> sympathy compression in MRVL/AVGO/MU/INTC overnight -> question: is this AMD-specific (execution) or AI-cycle (demand)? Until NVDA earnings (late May), market re-rates the second-derivative names lower while preserving Mag 7 leaders -> capex narrative bifurcates: hyperscalers still spending (META raised capex to $125-145B) but the chips winning that spend may consolidate to NVDA.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-listed semis bear the earnings impact; Asian fabs (TSM) and Korean memory (Samsung, Hynix) trade in sympathy on the Asia open; Taiwan and Korea ETFs (EWT, EWY) typically lag the move by one session.
macro_events.historical_analog: Cisco March 2000 — guidance miss ended the dot-com leadership though stock had already topped; Intel Oct 2000 PC warning kicked off the broader semi unwind; both signaled regime-changes when the second-derivative leader broke before the first.
macro_events.counterargument: AMD's drawdown could be the classic post-earnings overshoot — Meta's $60B commitment alone underwrites multi-year revenue; if NVDA confirms hyperscaler demand at its earnings, AMD could trace the 2024 NVDA pattern (panic gap, then 25% recovery in 8 weeks).

macro_events.title: Hormuz strait — Trump 'Project Freedom' meets renewed exchange of fire
macro_events.causal_chain: Trump's plan to escort ships through Hormuz is being tested as US/Iran forces traded shots; UAE oil-site drone strike spooked tanker insurance pools -> war-risk premium on VLCCs widens -> WTI rebounded above $100 from sub-$100 lows -> Brent $113 -> US gasoline approaching $5/gal national average per energy-sector commentary -> May CPI energy contribution will surprise high -> 10Y bid on safe-haven offsets the inflation impulse, leaving yields range-bound 4.40-4.60% -> Fed cut path delayed; first cut probability for July compresses below 50%.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: 21% of global oil and 20% of LNG flows through Hormuz; Asian refiners (China, India, Japan, Korea) reroute via Cape (+12-14 days, +$2M/cargo); European TTF gas vulnerable to Qatar LNG diversion; Gulf currencies (SAR, AED) pegged but local equity volatile.
macro_events.historical_analog: Sept 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24 hours, tankers ran +20-35% in a week; 1990 Gulf invasion — Brent doubled in 8 weeks; 2019 also saw equity downturn last 4-6 weeks before Fed-induced bounce.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran's 14-point ceasefire framework reportedly under review; if 'Project Freedom' escorts succeed for 2 weeks running, war-risk insurance unwinds quickly and Brent could collapse $15-20 in a month, pulling defense/tankers off highs.

macro_events.title: FOMC stays on hold; first 4-dissenter vote since 1992
macro_events.causal_chain: April 28-29 FOMC kept rate at 3.50-3.75% but vote was 8-4 — Governor Miran wanted -25bps, three other members objected to language hinting at eventual cuts -> committee fracture is the highest in 30+ years -> market reads as policy uncertainty premium -> 10Y holds 4.40s as both inflation-hedge and safe-haven bids cancel -> dollar firm at 98.5 -> credit spreads inch wider but not stressed -> equity multiples compress only at the margin (high-duration growth most exposed) -> if April CPI prints hot on May 12, dissent narrative flips: hawks gain control, terminal rate higher for longer.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: USD strength pressures EM; INR, IDR, TRY most exposed (oil importers, USD-debt heavy); EUR resilient at 1.08+; JPY weak but BoJ jaw-boning increased.
macro_events.historical_analog: October 1992 — last time 4 dissenters voted; preceded a meaningful regime change in policy stance; 2018 hiking cycle had Q4 dissent that signaled the eventual policy mistake.
macro_events.counterargument: If May 12 CPI core stays 2.6% YoY with energy as the only upside contributor, doves could regain consensus quickly — energy-driven inflation is typically 'looked through' historically.

macro_events.geographic_dimension: US tech leadership extends; ex-US tech (TCEHY, BABA) lagging; semiconductor exposure most concentrated in TSM (Taiwan) and KLAC/AMAT (US fab equipment).

macro_events.counterargument: AI demand may absorb every dollar of capex and then some; if NVDA prints another 70%+ growth quarter, the capex story re-validates and laggards (META, AMD) catch up.
